points.speaker: Jason Smith
points.quote:
Many Americans that are living with disabilities want to enter the 
workforce and seek gainful employment. In fact, an estimated 60 percent 
of Americans who receive benefits under the Social Security Disability 
Insurance program have stated a desire to return to work. Yet less than 
1 percent leave the disability insurance program each year for a job. 
That is a gigantic gap between the number of disabled Americans who 
want to work and the number who successfully return to work.
points.summary: Many Americans that are living with disabilities want to enter the workforce and seek gainful employment. In fact, an estimated 60 percent of Americans who receive benefits under the Social Security Disability Insurance program have stated a desire to return to work. Yet less than 1 percent leave the disability insurance program each year for a job. That is a gigantic gap between the number of disabled Americans who want to work and the number who successfully return to work.

points.speaker: Judy Chu
points.quote:
Mr. Speaker, at a time when Americans are dealing with skyrocketing 
prices and vulnerable populations like seniors and people with 
disabilities are struggling to get help with their Social Security 
benefits because this administration has created a customer service 
crisis through reckless staffing cuts, it is shameful that Republicans 
have chosen to bring H.R. 8884 to the floor. This bill won't lower 
costs, won't improve customer service, and won't make it easier for 
people with disabilities to access the benefits they have earned. 
Instead, it opens the door to cutting those benefits while making SSA's 
customer service crisis even worse.
points.summary: at a time when Americans are dealing with skyrocketing prices and vulnerable populations like seniors and people with disabilities are struggling to get help with their Social Security benefits because this administration has created a customer service crisis through reckless staffing cuts, it is shameful that Republicans have chosen to bring H.R. 8884 to the floor. This bill won't lower costs, won't improve customer service, and won't make it easier for people with disabilities to access the benefits they have earned. Instead, it opens the door to cutting those benefits while making SSA's customer service crisis even worse.

selection.reason: Directly supports the bill by showing a large unmet desire to work and a very low transition rate, motivating action.

selection.speaker: Jason Smith
selection.quote:
The Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act seeks to 
shrink that gap by simply restoring the Social Security 
Administration's authority to test drive solutions that can empower 
more of our fellow Americans to get back to work.
selection.summary: The Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act seeks to shrink that gap by simply restoring the Social Security Administration's authority to test drive solutions that can empower more of our fellow Americans to get back to work.
selection.reason: States the bill's purpose as reducing the work gap and empowering disabled Americans to return to work.

selection.speaker: Jason Smith
selection.quote:
Up until 2022, the SSA had such authority to run demonstration 
projects on improving work outcomes. With that authority expired and 
with so many disabled Americans still unable to successfully navigate 
the current program, we have to find a better way forward.
selection.summary: Up until 2022, the SSA had such authority to run demonstration projects on improving work outcomes. With that authority expired and with so many disabled Americans still unable to successfully navigate the current program, we have to find a better way forward.
selection.reason: Argues the bill is needed because the prior authority expired and current program barriers remain.

selection.speaker: Jason Smith
selection.quote:
In fact, some of the challenges cited for why so few SSDI 
beneficiaries successfully return to the workforce are confusing rules 
of the road for eligibility, that and a fear of overpayments and 
benefit cliffs.
selection.summary: In fact, some of the challenges cited for why so few SSDI beneficiaries successfully return to the workforce are confusing rules of the road for eligibility, that and a fear of overpayments and benefit cliffs.
selection.reason: Identifies specific barriers that the bill aims to address.

selection.speaker: Jason Smith
selection.quote:
Just so we do not forget why we should be focused on this issue, at a 
hearing of the Ways and Means Social Security and Work and Welfare 
Subcommittees in September, we heard from a witness, a former 
beneficiary, about how the work he found helped give his life real 
purpose and a different outlook. He was talking about the dignity of 
work, and that is what this bill will help deliver.
selection.summary: Just so we do not forget why we should be focused on this issue, at a hearing of the Ways and Means Social Security and Work and Welfare Subcommittees in September, we heard from a witness, a former beneficiary, about how the work he found helped give his life real purpose and a different outlook. He was talking about the dignity of work, and that is what this bill will help deliver.
selection.reason: Supports the bill by tying work to dignity and improved life purpose for beneficiaries.

selection.speaker: Jason Smith
selection.quote:
Representative Scott has been a long-time--and I would say long-time, 
tireless champion for Purple Heart veterans. Many of them wish to 
return to work but cannot afford the severe restrictions placed on 
their work status. I commend Mr. Scott for expanding his bill to allow 
the SSA's demonstration authority for so many impacted individuals, 
including blind Americans. He has identified a commonsense solution and 
is fighting to see it come to pass, just as it did through the Ways and 
Means Committee with bipartisan support.
selection.summary: Representative Scott has been a long-time--and I would say long-time, tireless champion for Purple Heart veterans. Many of them wish to return to work but cannot afford the severe restrictions placed on their work status. I commend Mr. Scott for expanding his bill to allow the SSA's demonstration authority for so many impacted individuals, including blind Americans. He has identified a commonsense solution and is fighting to see it come to pass, just as it did through the Ways and Means Committee with bipartisan support.
selection.reason: Explains that many veterans and blind Americans want to work but face severe restrictions, and endorses the solution.

selection.speaker: Danny K. Davis
selection.quote:
Mr. Speaker, I believe that you can measure the greatness of a 
society by how well it treats its old, how well it treats its young, 
and how well it treats those who have difficulties caring for 
themselves, through no fault of their own, yet need help from other 
elements of society.
selection.summary: Let me be clear that Democrats strongly support the goal of reducing unnecessary barriers for disabled Americans who want to explore returning to work. Over the years, Democrats many times have supported giving SSA this demonstration authority. However, the bill before us today tries to accomplish this worthwhile goal in the worst possible way.
selection.reason: Acknowledges the goal but explains the bill pursues it in a harmful way, supporting opposition.

selection.speaker: Judy Chu
selection.quote:
H.R. 8884, the Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act, 
aims to remove barriers to employment faced by individuals receiving 
Social Security Disability Insurance, or SSDI, benefits. It tries to do 
this by authorizing the Social Security Administration to conduct 
demonstration projects designed to test program changes that may 
encourage work.
selection.summary: Instead of protecting beneficiaries, it hands the Trump administration broad new authority to experiment with Social Security disability benefits with virtually no meaningful guardrails.
selection.reason: Focuses on the bill's dangerous lack of guardrails and risk to beneficiaries.

selection.speaker: Danny K. Davis
selection.quote:
If this bill is an indication of how we value our most vulnerable 
citizens, then we are not in good shape. Instead of going after 
billionaire tax cheats or ultrawealthy tax evaders, my Republican 
colleagues are advancing a bill that purports to remove barriers to 
work for disabled Americans.
selection.summary: First, let me be clear about what Social Security disability benefits are for. SSDI supports some of the most vulnerable Americans who have severe and long-lasting medical impairments that prevent them from being able to work at a level needed to financially support themselves.
selection.reason: Explains why these benefits are essential for vulnerable disabled people, grounding opposition to changes that could weaken them.

selection.speaker: Judy Chu
selection.quote:
Let me be clear that Democrats strongly support the goal of reducing 
unnecessary barriers for disabled Americans who want to explore 
returning to work. Over the years, Democrats many times have supported 
giving SSA this demonstration authority. However, the bill before us 
today tries to accomplish this worthwhile goal in the worst possible 
way.
selection.summary: SSDI is an earned benefit, with the average beneficiary having worked and paid into the system for 22 years before becoming disabled. It also has stringent eligibility criteria. To qualify, applicants must provide extensive medical evidence and undergo a rigorous eligibility determination process. Many applicants are initially denied and must appeal a process that often takes a year or more. Even after all levels of appeal, SSA typically finds only about one in three applicants eligible. SSDI benefits are extremely low, at an average of about $20,000 a year.
selection.reason: Highlights how hard-earned and modest the benefits are, supporting concern over exposing them to cuts.

selection.speaker: Danny K. Davis
selection.quote:
In all actuality, H.R. 8884 targets the earned benefits of workers 
who qualify for the Social Security Disability Insurance, SSDI.
selection.summary: The bottom line is that this administration cannot be trusted to not cut people's benefits. These are earned benefits that people with disabilities rely on to make ends meet. This bill puts that lifeline in jeopardy, and that is why this House should reject this bill.
selection.reason: States the core opposition: distrust of the administration and the danger the bill poses to a vital lifeline.

checks.reason: The summary faithfully preserves the quote’s claim about disabled Americans wanting to work, the 60 percent estimate, the less-than-1-percent exit rate, and the resulting gap.
The summary accurately states that the bill would restore SSA authority to test solutions to help more disabled Americans return to work.
The summary matches the quote’s point that the SSA had this demonstration authority until 2022 and now a better way forward is needed.
The summary correctly reproduces the cited obstacles: confusing eligibility rules, fear of overpayments, and benefit cliffs.
The summary faithfully reports the witness’s testimony that work gave his life purpose and that the bill helps deliver the dignity of work.
The summary adds several unsupported claims, including Purple Heart veterans, blind Americans, bipartisan committee action, and Scott expanding his bill beyond the quote.
Unsupported numeric/date expression or generic attribution.
The summary faithfully preserves the quote’s core claim that H.R. 8884 will not lower costs or improve customer service and instead risks cutting benefits and worsening SSA service.
The summary accurately captures that the bill gives the administration authority to run demonstration projects on Social Security disability benefits with limited guardrails.

The summary is about Democratic support for reducing barriers to work and bill criticism, but the quote is a generic statement about how society should treat vulnerable people, so the central claim is omitted.

The summary invents a specific explanation of SSDI’s purpose and beneficiaries that is not stated in the quote, which instead contrasts the bill with priorities like going after billionaire tax cheats.
The summary adds unsupported claims about the administration not being trusted and benefits being cut, while the quote only says the bill targets earned SSDI benefits.
